display.name: Google Drive
display.summary: Searches and reads the files shared with your service account, at any folder depth: Google Docs, Sheets and Slides, PDFs, and Word, Excel and PowerPoint files.
examples: What are the Q3 totals in the budget sheet?
Which files mention the pricing change?

fields.label: Service account key
fields.help: The JSON key file of a Google service account (the one Google Docs uses works too). Share the folders you want read with that account's email address. Its Google Cloud project needs the Google Drive API turned on.

agent.name: gdrive
agent.description: Searches and reads the files shared with the service account in Google Drive, at any folder depth: Google Docs, Sheets and Slides, PDFs, and Word, Excel and PowerPoint files -- specs, plans, proposals, budgets, trackers, meeting notes and decks that are not in the repository. A question naming a document without saying which system holds it may be here or in another document store: a filename does not say which, so ask every store.
agent.owns:
You own the files shared in Google Drive. Search first -- it reaches every file you can see, however deeply nested, and looks inside them -- and browse only to orient yourself. You do not own the source repository.

Every file and folder in a listing carries a link. When you report what a file says, GIVE THAT LINK with it: a Drive id is something you pass to read_drive_file, not something a reader can open.

A file marked "cannot be read" exists: say so, and never guess what is in it from its name.

tool_descriptions.browse_drive: List what is in Drive. Call with no folder_id to see what is shared with you, then call it again with a folder's id to see inside that folder. Files nested in subfolders are only visible by descending into them, so prefer search_drive when you know what you are looking for. Each file says what kind it is; one marked "cannot be read" exists, but its contents are not readable.
tool_descriptions.search_drive: Find files whose name or contents contain a word or phrase: Google Docs, Sheets and Slides, PDFs, and Word, Excel and PowerPoint files. This searches every file you can reach, however deeply nested, so it is the fastest way to locate material. Returns ids to pass to read_drive_file.
tool_descriptions.read_drive_file: Read the TEXT INSIDE one file, by the id shown by search_drive or browse_drive. Readable: Google Docs, Sheets and Slides; PDFs with selectable text; Word, Excel and PowerPoint; OpenDocument; CSV and plain text. A spreadsheet comes back one row per line with cells tab-separated, every sheet in turn. Not readable, and each says why rather than coming back empty: scanned PDFs, images, video, audio, forms, archives, old .doc/.xls/.ppt files, very large files, and files whose owner turned off downloading. When a file cannot be read, say it exists and its contents are not readable -- never guess them from its name.
